content: In 2016, Delamanid was provided to five patients at a hospital through the Otsuka company. Dr. Lawrence Mbuagbaw conducted a biostatistical consultation to support FDA reporting requirements for the use of Bedaquiline, a project funded by Janssen Pharmaceuticals. Dr. Anuj K. Bhatnagar served as the Co-Principal Investigator for the STREAM 2 trial at the Rajan Babu Institute of Pulmonary Medicine and Tuberculosis (RBI PMT) in Delhi, India, which began in March 2019. The trial's financial aspects, including ward refurbishment, equipment upgrades, staff hiring, laboratory improvements, and patient support, were managed by Vital Strategies, an affiliate of the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (IUATLD). No direct funds were transferred to the institute for this trial. The National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (NIRT) in Chennai, under the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), initiated a Phase 3 trial called BEAT TB to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of newer drug combinations for pre-XDR and XDR-TB across five sites in India. At the RBI PMT site, where Dr. Bhatnagar is the Principal Investigator, the site initiation visit and recruitment of personnel were recently completed. The first grant installment for this trial was allocated for staff recruitment, equipment, laboratory reagents, and patient and DOT provider support. Amrita Daftary, a consultant at Columbia University from 2016 to 2021, provided qualitative expertise for designing and evaluating adherence interventions for XDR-TB-HIV patients in South Africa. She also conducted research on engaging pharmacy providers in India for TB screening and referral and led observational studies on TB care quality in South Africa. Her work was funded by IC-IMPACTS, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), and the NIH. David Dowdy received research funding from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, totaling approximately $300,000 annually, and travel support of $10,000 for attending meetings. Gabriela Gomez worked as a consultant providing modeling results for a universal TB drug regimen investment case, funded by BMGF and MSF. She also managed research grants for economic evaluations of TB regimens, including the BPaL regimen, before joining Sanofi Pasteur in 2019. Dr. Richard Menzies conducted WHO-commissioned evidence reviews for MDR-TB treatment guidelines. Rada Savic received research funding from NIH, UNITAID, and BMGF for TB-related studies and served on advisory committees for TB Alliance and other organizations. Zarir Udwadia facilitated access to Bedaquiline and Delamanid for patients through compassionate use programs without financial transactions. Andrew Vernon led a clinical research group at the US CDC conducting TB trials, including studies on Rifapentine and Levofloxacin. The WHO Guideline Development Group (GDG) and Evidence Review Group (ERG) members declared their interests transparently. Interests were assessed for potential conflicts, and significant conflicts led to exclusion from the GDG. The GDG included diverse representatives from academia, technical partners, civil society, and professional organizations. All members completed WHO Declaration of Interest forms, and their biographies were made public before meetings. External reviewers and evidence reviewers also declared no conflicting interests related to the guidelines' objectives.
